cases.question: Explain Yao’s final vote for the 2023 accelerated ZEV sales mandate and compare it to current broad EV-promotion messaging. The 2023 law targeted 100% new light-duty sales by 2035, not banning existing cars or requiring everyone to own an EV. Crucially the April2026 government announcement AND current captured consolidated Act soften the 2035 target to75%; Yao has no indexed vote on that revision. Do not pretend his past vote establishes support for the current75% target or all climate/LNG policy. Note rural cost and readiness arguments as arguments, not established harms. Inconclusive on alignment with the precise present policy is appropriate.

unassessed_commitments.summary: Coordinate regional surgical waitlists and add eight MRI machines and ten CT scanners.
unassessed_commitments.quote: eight new MRI machines and 10 CT scanners
unassessed_commitments.reason: The reviewed regulatory vote does not approve these facilities or demonstrate shorter waits. These are new promises after the collected voting record ends in April 2024.

unassessed_commitments.summary: Suspend part of the gas tax and introduce pricing rules to lower fuel costs.
unassessed_commitments.quote: suspend a portion of the provincial gas tax
unassessed_commitments.reason: The used-car tax vote concerns a different tax and an earlier period. It cannot establish delivery of this new gas-price plan or its advertised savings.

unassessed_commitments.quote: B.C. and Canadian-made goods and materials
